## Data analysis

Descriptive data are presented as mean and standard deviations (SD). For inferential statistics, Bayesian models were constructed using the Stan probabilistic programming language [@stanpaper] and fitted using the `cmdstanr` interface [@cmdstanr] in R [@R]. All sampling from the prior and joint posterior distribution was done using the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) no-U-turn sampler ([Stan Reference Manual: MCMC sampling](https://mc-stan.org/docs/reference-manual/mcmc.html)). Performance of the HMC algorithm was assessed by inspecting chain convergence statistics (R-hat) and visually inspecting convergence and stationary sampling across multiple HMC chains. A general workflow was adopted where models were incrementally built and tested for validity through simulations. First, implications of prior distributions were evaluated using prior predictive simulations. Priors where selected to constrain model predictions and parameter values to *a priori* plausible ranges. This approach encourage the use of weakly informative priors on model parameters which regularizes models and provide shrinkage of estimates and predictions without distorting the influence of the data on inference [@lemoine2019,@mcelreath2020,@gelman2014]. Synthetic data was used to confirm to that models were not misspecified. Samples from the joint posterior distribution sampled using observed data were used to create posterior predictive checks where model implications are simulated and compared to characteristics of the observed data [@gelman2014, pp. 141]. Selected models were also assessed for inferential capabilities using synthetic data simulations where parameter values are known. Sensitivity of model specifications on inference was assessed by comparing predictions from different models.
 

## Description of the data set and participants

The overall objective of the present analysis is to determine the effect of N-3 supplementation in combination with resistance training on indications of metabolic health. Outcome variables in the analysis are:

- Metabolic syndrome (derived from sub-scores; *primary*)
   * Triglycerides
   * Waist circumference
   * Blood pressure 
   * HDL Cholesterol
   * Resting glucose
- Body mass index
- Relative fat mass
- HOMA2-IR
- OGTT
- Adiponectin
- Fatty acid composition

```{r}

# Source figure options, packages, and main data prep.
source("./R/fig-opt-fun.R")
source("./R/packages.R")
source("./R/data-prep.R")
source("./R/helpers.R")

# Settings
refit.models <- FALSE

```



```{r}
#| label: data-prep-participants




part <- AOData::idkeys  
  
## Descriptives data 
baseline_dat <- AOData::bodycomp |>
  select(participant, time, lean.whole, BMC.whole, fat.whole)  |>
  mutate(weight = lean.whole + BMC.whole + fat.whole) |>
  inner_join(part) |>
  filter(time == "T1") |>
  ## Calculate height based on weight (DXA) and BMI 
  mutate(height = 100 * sqrt((weight/1000) / bmi)) |>
  ## Calculate relative lean and fat
  mutate(lean.rel = 100 * (lean.whole / weight), 
         fat.rel = 100 * (fat.whole/weight), 
         # Weight in kg
         weight = weight / 1000) |>
  select(participant, 
         treat, 
         completed, 
         sex, 
         age, 
         height, 
         weight, 
         bmi) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = age:bmi)
  
  
## Included participants 
total_participants <- baseline_dat |> 
  distinct(participant) |> 
  pull(participant)




# Per completed period
# dat |> 
#   summarise(.by = c(completed, treat, sex, name), 
#             m = mean(value), 
#             s = sd(value), 
#             min = min(value), 
#             max = max(value))
  
# Total

# Calculate n
n_total <- baseline_dat |> 
  filter(name == "age") |> 
  summarise(.by = c(treat, sex), 
            n = n()) 

n_male_omega <- n_total[1,3][[1]]
n_female_omega <- n_total[3,3][[1]]
n_male_ctrl <-  n_total[2,3][[1]]
n_female_ctrl <-  n_total[4,3][[1]]

N <- sum(n_total$n)
```

A total of `r N` participants are included in the data analysis. Participants were randomized into two groups, an active treatment-group (N-3 fatty acids, XX mg day^-1^) and a placebo control group (Placebo; @tbl-participants).



```{r}
#| label: tbl-participants
#| tbl-cap: "Participant characteristics."


baseline_dat |> 
  summarise(.by = c(treat, sex, name), 
            m = mean(value), 
            s = sd(value), 
            min = min(value), 
            max = max(value), 
            n = n()) |> 
  mutate(stats = paste0(
    sprintf("%.0f", round(m, 0)), 
    " (", 
    sprintf("%.0f", round(s, 0)), 
    ") [",
    sprintf("%.0f", round(min, 0)), 
    " - ", 
    sprintf("%.0f", round(max, 0)), 
    "]"), 
    n = n) |> 
  
  dplyr::select(treat, sex, name,n, stats) |> 
  

  
  dplyr::select(-n) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = treat, 
              values_from = stats) |> 
  
  mutate(sex = if_else(sex == "m", "Male", "Female"), 
         name = case_when(
           name == "age" ~ "Age (years)", 
           name == "height" ~ "Stature (cm)", 
           name == "weight" ~ "Body mass (kg)", 
           name == "bmi" ~ "Body mass index (kg&times;m^-2^)", 
           TRUE ~ NA )) |> 

  group_by(sex) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_markdown() |> 
  
  cols_label(omega = md(paste0("N-3<br>(&male; n = ", 
                               n_male_omega, 
                               "; &female; n = ", 
                               n_female_omega, ")")),
             ctrl = md(paste0("Placebo<br>(&male; n = ", 
                              n_male_ctrl, 
                              "; &female; n = ",
                              n_female_ctrl, ")")), 
             sex = "", 
             name = "") |> 
  tab_footnote(footnote = "Data are presnted as Mean (SD) [Min-Max]")

```
